analysis: Both supplied units are BASE-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 3700-4194) holding historical release notes for v0.9.x. The PR patch for this file is documentation only: it replaces the v0.10.8 candidate heading with v0.10.9 and adds upgrade and rollout notes, with changed head lines 11-400. The patch excerpt is truncated, so I could not see the whole head change. No executable code, configuration, protocol, authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or storage logic is changed in the supplied evidence. The visible added text is operator guidance on pair upgrades and on recovering serving. It includes `darkbloom stop --solo`, `darkbloom cluster pair --forget <pin>` and a correction of earlier advice about plain `darkbloom stop`. I identified no new attack surface, no weakened mitigation and no invalidated assumption for T-041, TB-011, TB-012 or TB-014. The base excerpts mention prefix-cache, App Attest and lifecycle items, but they are unchanged historical text and are not new behavior. Remaining uncertainty: the rest of the head changelog beyond the truncated excerpt, and any code changes in other batches that the 0.10.9 pair/lock fixes describe. I did not review those. Integration should check that code behind the pair serving-lock and updater claims honors the stated custody and authorization boundaries, since this changelog is not evidence of the code's behavior.
